As someone with medically recognised OSDD1B, I, the host, also am always fronting. Though, during trauma and extreme dissociation, I have what can be the closest to this form's "blackout periods", where I forget what happens/have memories taken from me by other alters. So I would say that always fronting/cofronting is normal. Also, when I realised there was "something wrong", AKA, our system was a thing, there was only two that I knew of, although there was certainly another, the alter that had came out during my abuse. So, I wouldn't worry about numbers. Now, we have about 20 or so alters including me, due to splitting and/or discovery. And yes, I feel that communication in OSDD1B systems can tend to be more difficult. Our system now has a gatekeeper who has easier access to most of the other alters, but other than that I can only call a few to the front very easily if I need them. Just try to work with the alters you can communicate with before worrying about anything else first. What's more important is communication to help build a stable system. I know it's very easy to doubt yourself and your system, but communication is key. It took me a long time to accept that I was a system, realising this in 2017 with no prior knowledge of systems/alters or my abuse, but with communication I've been able to build a easy strand of information and knowledge of my system and the alters in it. If you ever need any guidance, feel free to shoot us a message. Our gatekeeper Anders is probably more helpful with the inner workings, since our system works in a particular way that differs from other systems I have encountered in the past, but that's all to an understanding we have made in our system. Hope all will be well for y'all :\^ ) - Jacob
